_comment: V-OBS-008 -- a journaled Secret pre-state is digest-only, and the replayer recognises it as such (05 §1.2). Two halves, and the second is why the check exists: journal.Sanitize WRITES the `sha256:` marker and undo.RedactedSecretKeys READS it, across a package boundary neither side's suite crosses. M5 and M6 break one end each. Only ./internal/journal/ runs, which is deliberate -- the undo-side mutants must be caught by the journal-side test that joins them, not by undo's own suite.

mutants.why: server-side-apply bookkeeping stays in the snapshot, dwarfing the object and pushing honest snapshots over the inline limit
the annotation is a second, UNDIGESTED copy of the Secret; leaving it makes the redaction cosmetic
stringData holds material as written rather than base64, so skipping it puts plaintext straight into etcd

edits.find:
for _, field := range []string{"data", "stringData"} {
			raw, found, err := unstructured.NestedMap(out.Object, field)
edits.replace:
for _, field := range []string{"data"} {
			raw, found, err := unstructured.NestedMap(out.Object, field)

mutants.why: a digest over the key name still looks per-key and still redacts, but two keys holding the same credential no longer agree -- so no candidate value can ever be proved to be the right one at restore
the journal still redacts, but the rollback replayer no longer recognises the redaction and applies the digests as if they were values -- destroying the credential and reporting a completed undo
the same divergence from the other end: undo stops looking for what the journal writes, and every journaled Secret becomes replayable as digests
a redacted stringData key is not reported, so the replayer refuses on some keys of a Secret and silently writes hex into the rest
the whole redaction is skipped and the Secret is journaled as material, which is the failure the requirement exists to prevent
over-stripping is the other way to be wrong: an undo that restored an object without its annotations restores a different object
